patch.value: The release Sentry gate blocks on a resolved issue that regressed only through environment=test events, because it judges test traffic per issue instead of per regression

Observed 2026-11-28. Blocker #1794's blocker_retry run 46149734279 failed at the sentry-telemetry-gate on PM-CLI-42. The issue had been resolved at 13:25Z after its two automation events (11-26, 11-27) were explained. At 13:39Z, four new events from a pm-github reproduction harness arrived correctly labelled environment=test, and they regressed it. pm-usn5k2 made the gate drop an unresolved issue only when a complete listing of issues with any non-test event (!environment:test !pm.source_context:test, at any time) lacks it. PM-CLI-42 still has its old automation events, so its test-only regression counts as release-blocking. Today's retry marker was then spent, so the day's release needed an operator dispatch and a time-boxed archive. Expected: a regression is judged by the events since the issue was last resolved. When every event after the last resolution is test traffic (environment test or pm.source_context test), the issue is test-only for the gate. An issue never resolved, a regression with any non-test event, or a lookup that fails or is incomplete keeps blocking (fail closed). Duplicate check: searched 'sentry gate test-only regression resolved issue environment test events'. pm-usn5k2 (closed) owns the per-issue test-only rule, and no item owns post-resolution judgement.

An unresolved issue whose events since its last resolution are all environment=test or pm.source_context=test is reported as test-only and does not block; A never-resolved issue, a regression with any non-test event since the resolution, and a failed or truncated activity or event lookup keep blocking; The gate spec covers each case with mocked Sentry responses, and a live gate run reports the classification
A resolved issue that regresses only through test events no longer blocks the daily release, while any non-test regression still does

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Implementation note (2026-11-28): after the pm-usn5k2 partition, excludeTestOnlyRegressions judges every remaining issue whose substatus is regressed. It reads the issue's activity (GET /organizations/{org}/issues/{id}/), takes the latest set_resolved* entry, then lists non-test events since then (GET .../issues/{id}/events/?query=!environment:test !pm.source_context:test&start=<resolution>&end=<now>&per_page=1). An empty list moves the issue to test_only and reports it under ignored_test_only_regression_short_ids. It fails closed when the activity has no resolution, when the details or events request is not OK or throws, when the body is empty or not a list, and when the listing came through the sentry CLI with no API token. Live API probe on PM-CLI-42: the activity shows set_resolved 13:27:21Z and set_regression 13:39:40Z, the non-test event list since 13:30Z holds 0 events and the one since 11-27 holds 1 (the automation event), so the rule would have skipped today's test-only regression. A live gate run against the project now reports ok with ignored_test_only_regression_short_ids []. PM-CLI-42 is archived until 02:59Z, so it is not listed.

patch.value: PM-CLI-42-like regressions made of environment=test events do not block, while any non-test regression still does

The Sentry release gate judges a regressed issue by its events since its latest resolution, read from the issue's activity and the filtered event list. A regression made only of test traffic is skipped and reported under ignored_test_only_regression_short_ids. Every other case fails closed: no resolution, a non-test event since it, a failed or malformed lookup, or a CLI listing without an API token.

Gate spec: of 10 regressed or ongoing issues, only the one with no non-test event since its latest resolution is skipped. The other 9 (real regression, no resolution, malformed activity, details 500, events 500, events throw, non-list body, empty body, ongoing) block, and a CLI listing keeps blocking with no fetch. The live API probe confirms the queries return 0 since today's resolution and 1 before it, and 76 gate tests pass with 100% coverage of the changed lines
A resolved issue that regressed only through test events no longer blocks the release gate

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 1, gpt-6.2-sol xhigh, 2026-11-28. Both findings were valid and are fixed. P1: a production event timestamped ahead of the gate's clock could mark the issue regressed yet fall after the event query's end, so an empty list was not proof. The gate now reads the set_regression activity's data.event_id and requires that triggering event itself to be test traffic (environment or pm.source_context test). The window starts at the earlier of the resolution and the trigger, and ends 10 minutes past max(now, trigger, issue lastSeen). P2: Promise.all fired one issue-details request per regression, against Sentry's 5 GETs per second per organization. Lookups now run one at a time within one budget, and a 429 is retried up to 3 times after its Retry-After (1 s when absent or invalid) unless that would pass the budget. Each of these failure modes keeps the issue blocking. The spec has 19 fixture issues, covering throttled retries, an exhausted throttle, a Retry-After past the budget and a 429 with no header.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 2, 2026-11-28: three findings, valid, settled by principle. The gate may skip a regression only when it can prove that every non-test event was already judged when the issue was resolved, and event timestamps cannot prove that. (1) P1: a production event received after the resolution but stamped before it escaped a timestamp window. The rule now reads RECEIPT time: one page (per_page 100, full=true) of the issue's non-test events from firstSeen minus 1 h to now plus 1 h, and every event's dateReceived must precede the latest resolution. A missing dateReceived or a second page keeps the issue blocking. This subsumes the round-1 trigger-event check, which was removed. (2) P2: a newer set_regression with an unreadable date fell back to the older cycle. Now any undated resolution or regression transition makes the feed unorderable and keeps the issue blocking. (3) P2: Math.max(1, ...) still started requests after the budget was spent. fetchSentryPage now checks the deadline before each request and refuses a response that arrives after it, and a spec proves the next issue's lookup never starts.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: CodeRabbit review on PR #1795, 2026-11-28, two Minor findings, both valid. The deadline-before-fetch finding was already fixed in Codex round 2. A 429 on the final attempt used to wait its Retry-After and then give up. Now the last attempt returns at once (SENTRY_LOOKUP_ATTEMPTS = 3, a for(;;) loop with no unreachable tail).

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 3, 2026-11-28: four gate findings. Three fixed: (a) a regression stamped at the resolution's own instant is not ordered after it, so the comparison is now strict (>); (b) the deadline is re-checked after the body is read and parsed, so a page read after the budget is refused; (c) timestamps are parsed only when they are strings (parseSentryTime), because Date.parse coerces a one-element array. Declined, with reason: 'route regressed issues through the proof before the test-only exclusion'. pm-usn5k2 drops an issue only when the COMPLETE non-test listing lacks it, which means the issue has no non-test event at all. Such an issue is test-only by definition, whatever its activity says, so a proof lookup adds nothing and its failure must not make the issue block.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 4, 2026-11-28: three gate findings, all fixed. (a) Timestamps must be ISO 8601 strings with a zone (SENTRY_TIMESTAMP), because Date.parse reads a bare '0' as a year; a sub-millisecond tie fails closed. (b) Pagination: the shared nextSentryPage regex needs rel then results, in that order. The regression lookup now uses sentryLinkHasNextPage, which reads parameters in any order: a present header without a readable next link, or with any value but results="false", counts as more pages. (c) Sentry caps full=true event pages at 10 whatever per_page says, so the limit is 10 and the docs say so. An issue with more non-test events keeps blocking (fail closed).

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 5, 2026-11-28: three gate findings, all fixed. (a) Only a MISSING Link header means one page. A present header proves the last page only with a well-formed next link (<target>) whose results are "false", so a blank or targetless header keeps the issue blocking. (b) Timestamps must name a real calendar instant: isRealCalendarTime checks month, day-in-month and the clock, since Date.parse rolls 2026-02-30 into March. (c) Retry-After is read as delay seconds or as an HTTP date (delay = max(0, date - now)), with 1 s otherwise.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 6, 2026-11-28: two P2s and one P3, all fixed. (a) The Link header must hold exactly one next link with a <target> and exactly one results marker, and that marker must be "false". Conflicting markers or two next links count as more pages. (b) An issue-details response that advertises another page is not the whole activity history, so the issue keeps blocking. (c) Retry-After dates are read only in GMT forms (RFC 9110). A zone-less asctime date would be read in the runner's local time, so it falls back to 1 s.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 7, 2026-11-28. Settled the remaining parser class by one principle: only Sentry's exact wire shapes are evidence, and anything else is unproven, so the issue keeps blocking. Concretely: a Link header must consist only of entries in the strict grammar <target>(; key="value")*, so unquoted rel=next or rel="next"x fails it; exactly one rel="next" with exactly one results="false". The response status must be exactly 200, so a 206 Partial Content is not evidence. Retry-After is read only as delay seconds or an IMF-fixdate (RFC 9110 preferred form); slash, zone-less and asctime forms fall back to 1 s. A body finished at the deadline instant is refused (>=).

value.text: CodeRabbit review of e869f0d49, 2026-11-28, Major, valid, settled by principle: the regression window must not depend on any value that can move. The listed firstSeen goes back when an older event arrives, so a late production event stamped before it could escape a firstSeen-bound query. The lookup now reads non-test events from now minus 90 days (Sentry's longest retention) to now plus 1 h, and no longer reads firstSeen at all. The 10-event page cap still fails closed for busier issues. Also: CodeRabbit flagged the spec's fetch-mock callback at cognitive complexity 17 to 20 (sonarjs runs on tests/** in Gates (static), which failed on bfe291642). The fixture is now split into fixtureResponse, eventsResponse and issueResponse, and repo-wide pnpm lint:eslint is clean.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 8, 2026-11-28. Two P2s and two P3s, all fixed. (a) Sentry reads !environment:test as environment != 'test', which also drops events with no environment, so a non-test event without an environment received after the resolution could be missed (fail open). The lookup now filters only on !pm.source_context:test, where a missing tag reads as empty and stays, and sets test traffic aside by each event's own tags (isTestTrafficEvent). An event without readable tags counts as non-test. (b) Each Link entry must carry exactly one rel, so rel="previous"; rel="next" counts as more pages. (c) The window's lower bound is padded for clock skew as well. (d) An IMF-fixdate Retry-After must round-trip through toUTCString, which rejects 30 Feb and a mismatched weekday.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 9 (scoped to real-world triggers), 2026-11-28, P1, valid and fixed: Sentry records the regression and its triggering event id before the event is indexed, so during indexing lag the event list can hold only pre-resolution events while a production event has already reopened the issue. The gate now reads the latest set_regression's data.event_id, fetches that event by id under the same budget (GET .../issues/{id}/events/{event_id}/), and requires it to be test traffic by its own tags. A missing id, an unindexed (404) event or a non-test trigger keeps the issue blocking. This restores the round-1 trigger check on top of the receipt-time rule.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 10, 2026-11-28, P2, valid and fixed by principle: the proof covers only the issue as it was resolved. A merge, unmerge_source, unmerge_destination or reprocess activity after the latest resolution brings in events whose receipt times predate the resolution although that resolution never judged them, so such activity keeps the issue blocking. The same activity before the resolution was judged.

value.author: harness:claude-code
value.text: Codex review round 11 (final verification, P0-P1 only), 2026-11-28, one P1, valid: Sentry records a merge activity when it queues the move, and a worker moves the events later, so a merge stamped before the resolution can still bring in unjudged production events after it. Closed by principle: an issue whose event set was ever regrouped (any merge, unmerge_source, unmerge_destination or reprocess activity) is never waived and keeps blocking. Regrouped issues are rare, so the cost is small.

value.text: Codex review round 12 (P0-P1 only), 2026-11-28, one P1, valid: Sentry's issue-details endpoint silently caps the activity array with no Link header, so an older merge can drop out of view while the latest resolution and regression stay visible. The gate now needs POSITIVE evidence of a complete feed: the feed is newest-first and its oldest entry is always the issue's first_seen, so the feed counts as whole only when that entry is present (PM-CLI-42's live feed has it). Otherwise the issue keeps blocking.
